summary: Our project is an interactive digital space museum designed to bring the rich histories of NASA’s inactive spacecraft to life for school-age students. Built as a free static website using React and Vite, the platform features an interactive space map, clickable hardware diagrams, and "Wake the Explorer" visualizations. To solve the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge, we translated dense technical data from NASA archives into engaging, accessible stories about legacy equipment left on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space. Rather than viewing these machines as discarded trash, our museum frames them as monuments of human ingenuity, helping young space fans connect with the groundbreaking science that shaped our understanding of the solar system.
details:
Project Overview

Our project is a digital space museum that functions as a free static website. It features an interactive space map, clickable hardware diagrams, "Where are they now?" timelines, and a unique "Wake the Explorer" visualization. We tell the stories of legacy spacecraft across the Moon, Mars, the Asteroid belt, and deep space. For each piece of equipment, our platform details who it was, why it was sent, how the hardware functioned, what scientific discoveries it made, and its final status.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Engaging Education: We take the rich histories of discarded space equipment out of dense textbooks and technical websites and translate them into engaging stories for school-age students.
  • Changing Perspectives: By highlighting these "quiet sentinels," we aim to show that these inactive machines are not trash, but operational relics and monuments to human exploration that forever changed planetary science.
  • Accessibility: The website prioritizes user experience and accessibility, featuring keyboard-friendly navigation and reduced-motion options.
  • Reliability: Each explorer profile provides direct links back to official NASA sources to ensure accurate and verifiable information.

Tools & Technologies Used

  • Frameworks: The application was built using React and Vite.
  • Original Graphics: All graphics are 100% original and created using CSS and SVG, deliberately avoiding the use of NASA logos or AI-generated images and video.
  • Data Sources: Information was strictly sourced from NASA mission pages (science.nasa.gov) and the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA).
  • AI Assistance: AI tools (Claude, Anthropic) were utilized strictly to help generate code and draft text.

Creativity & Future Vision

Our project creatively reframes abandoned equipment as a curated, interactive museum experience rather than a static list of facts. Features like the "Wake the Explorer" visualization offer an imaginative, interactive way for users to engage with dormant spacecraft. Looking forward, we have planned for scalable growth by outlining a "teacher mode" with short quizzes, expanding to include multiple languages for global accessibility, and adding more legacy spacecraft such as the Apollo Lunar Module stages, InSight, and Viking.
